recipes.name: BAZAAR
recipes.summary: inventory, and fulfilment only on a received payment
recipes.legacy: The shop posts inventory changes, HMAC-signed with `SHOP_HMAC`, to `/in/shop`; the warehouse system takes fulfilment releases on its API.
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each inventory change becomes a `bazaar.inventory_level` attestation. TheProtocol's own `payment.received` webhook (signed by the registry) is forwarded to the WMS with the payer, the amount and the ledger transaction: the WMS fulfils only what has been paid, and a payment that never settles never reaches it.
recipes.needs: An agent with the `attestor` role; a webhook for `payment.received` registered in the console (Developer, Webhooks) pointing at the proxy's `/in/theprotocol`, its secret as `TP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and the shop agent's DID in the `paid-release` mapping's `when` (the owner's webhook carries the income of every agent the owner has); `SHOP_HMAC`, `WMS_HMAC`, and the WMS endpoint in the sink's `url`. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: a receiver never finishes, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/mock_wms.py --listen 127.0.0.1:8721` is a WMS; `python fake/fake_shop.py http://127.0.0.1:8711/in/shop --count 4` posts four inventory changes. Then:
recipes.check: The WMS's file (`wms-received.jsonl`) holds one release per payment received.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# BAZAAR (the marketplace blueprint): the shop's inventory changes become signed attestations on TheProtocol, and the
# warehouse (WMS) is told to fulfil only when a buyer's payment has arrived: TheProtocol's own payment.received webhook,
# signed by the registry, is forwarded to the WMS with the payer, the amount and the ledger transaction, and the WMS
# matches it to its open order. A payment that never settles never reaches the WMS.
#
# The shop side: POST /in/shop, HMAC-signed with SHOP_HMAC (fake/fake_shop.py). TheProtocol's side: register this
# proxy's /in/theprotocol as a webhook for payment.received in the console (Developer, Webhooks) and give its secret as
# TP_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The WMS side: the sink's url, checking X-Signature-256 with WMS_HMAC (fake/mock_wms.py).
version: 1
name: bazaar-shop
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/bazaar-state.db
sources:
  shop:
    type: webhook
    config: {listen: "0.0.0.0:8711", path: /in/shop, id_field: event_id, secret: env:SHOP_HMAC}
  theprotocol:
    type: theprotocol_events
    config: {listen: "0.0.0.0:8712", path: /in/theprotocol, secret: env:TP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, events: [payment.received]}
actions:
  attest:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: bazaar.inventory_level}
    limits: {per_minute: 300}
sinks:
  wms:
    type: webhook
    # your warehouse system's fulfilment endpoint (a URL, written here; its signing secret by reference)
    config: {url: "https://wms.example.com/api/v1/fulfilment-releases", secret: env:WMS_HMAC, timeout_s: 15}
mappings:
  - name: inventory
    version: 1
    from: shop
    to: attest
    when: {path: $.payload.kind, equals: inventory}
    fields:
      sku: $.payload.sku
      on_hand: $.payload.on_hand
      warehouse: $.payload.warehouse
      at: $.payload.at
  - name: paid-release
    version: 1
    from: theprotocol
    to: wms
    # the owner's webhook carries the income of every agent the owner has: release goods for the shop's own (its DID)
    when: {path: $.payload.agent_did, equals: "did:theprotocol:your-shop-agent"}
    fields:
      seller_agent: $.payload.agent_did
      payer: $.payload.from_did
      amount: $.payload.amount
      currency: $.payload.currency
      ledger_tx: $.payload.ledger_txid
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

table.out: fulfilment releases to the WMS, only once paid

recipes.name: DYNAMO
recipes.legacy: Smart meters publish JSON readings (`seq`, `kwh`, `voltage`, `at`) to `meters/<meter>/reading` on the plant's broker (QoS 1).
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each reading becomes a `dynamo.meter_reading` attestation, the meter taken from the topic; a redelivered message is kept once (the meter's `seq` is the id).
recipes.needs: An agent with the `attestor` role; the broker's address, and in production its CA and a client certificate (`tls`). Install the `proxy-mqtt` extra. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: a receiver never finishes, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `docker run -d -p 1883:1883 eclipse-mosquitto:2 mosquitto -c /mosquitto-no-auth.conf` is a broker; `python fake/fake_meters.py --meters 3 --readings 4` publishes twelve readings. Then:
recipes.check: `tp-proxy status` shows the readings sent; the attestations are on the agent's record.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# DYNAMO (the energy blueprint): smart meters publish their readings to the plant's MQTT broker; every reading becomes
# a signed attestation on TheProtocol (the meter is the topic's second level, meters/<meter>/reading), kept exactly once
# however often the broker redelivers it (QoS 1, a persistent session, the meter's own sequence number as the id).
#
# The meter side: JSON {"seq", "kwh", "voltage", "at"} on meters/<meter>/reading (fake/fake_meters.py publishes such
# readings). Production brokers use TLS with a client certificate: uncomment tls and name the files.
version: 1
name: dynamo-meters
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/dynamo-state.db
sources:
  meters:
    type: mqtt
    config:
      host: broker.plant.local
      port: 1883
      client_id: tp-proxy-dynamo-meters      # the broker keeps this source's session under this name
      topics: [{filter: "meters/+/reading", qos: 1}]
      id_field: $.seq                        # each meter's own reading number
      # tls: {ca_file: /etc/tp-proxy/plant-ca.crt, cert_file: /etc/tp-proxy/meters.crt, private_key: file:/etc/tp-proxy/meters.key}
actions:
  attest:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: dynamo.meter_reading}
    limits: {per_minute: 600}
sinks: {}
mappings:
  - name: reading
    version: 1
    from: meters
    to: attest
    fields:
      meter: $.payload.levels.1
      reading: $.payload.data.seq
      kwh: $.payload.data.kwh
      voltage: {path: $.payload.data.voltage, default: null}
      at: $.payload.data.at
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

recipes.name: HANSA
recipes.summary: gate-out events to attestations, the ERP receives the chain
recipes.legacy: The terminal operating system posts each gate event, HMAC-signed with `GATE_HMAC`, to `/in/gate`.
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each gate-OUT becomes a `hansa.gate_out` attestation, and the ERP's API receives one signed POST per event, the record's key as its `Idempotency-Key`.
recipes.needs: An agent with the `attestor` role; `GATE_HMAC` shared with the TOS, `ERP_HMAC` with the ERP; the ERP's endpoint written in the sink's `url`. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: a receiver never finishes, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/mock_erp.py --listen 127.0.0.1:8720` is an ERP that checks the signature and keeps each event once; `python fake/fake_tos.py http://127.0.0.1:8711/in/gate --count 6` posts six events (two gate-INs, not attested). Then:
recipes.check: The ERP's file (`erp-received.jsonl`) holds each gate-out once; the attestations are on the agent's record.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# HANSA (the port-logistics blueprint): the terminal operating system (TOS) posts each gate event, HMAC-signed, to the
# proxy; every gate-OUT becomes a signed attestation on TheProtocol, and the ERP receives the chain on its API: one
# signed POST per event, the record's key as its Idempotency-Key, so the ERP keeps each event once.
#
# The TOS side: POST /in/gate with X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC of the body> (fake/fake_tos.py does it). The ERP
# side: the sink's url, checking X-Signature-256 with ERP_HMAC (fake/mock_erp.py is such an ERP).
version: 1
name: hansa-gate
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/hansa-state.db
sources:
  tos:
    type: webhook
    config: {listen: "0.0.0.0:8711", path: /in/gate, id_field: event_id, secret: env:GATE_HMAC}
actions:
  attest:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: hansa.gate_out}
    limits: {per_minute: 300}
sinks:
  erp:
    type: webhook
    # your ERP's endpoint for gate events (a URL, written here; its signing secret by reference)
    config: {url: "https://erp.example.com/api/v1/gate-events", secret: env:ERP_HMAC, timeout_s: 15}
    limits: {per_minute: 300}
mappings:
  - name: gate-out
    version: 1
    from: tos
    to: attest
    when: {path: $.payload.status, equals: OUT}
    fields:
      container: $.payload.container_id
      gate: $.payload.gate
      truck: $.payload.truck_plate
      at: $.payload.timestamp
      seal: {path: $.payload.seal, default: null}
      terminal: HAM-CTA
  - name: gate-out-to-erp
    version: 1
    from: tos
    to: erp
    when: {path: $.payload.status, equals: OUT}
    fields:
      container: $.payload.container_id
      gate: $.payload.gate
      at: $.payload.timestamp
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
breaker: {refusals: 5, failures: 10, cooldown_s: 30}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

recipes.name: KEYSTONE
recipes.summary: a passed test run as a milestone's evidence
recipes.legacy: The site's sensor logger exports each test run as a CSV to an SFTP server (`/exports`, a `.done` marker once complete): measurement rows, then an acceptance row (passed) or a rejection row (failed) naming the contract and its milestone.
recipes.on_theprotocol: A passed run's acceptance row is delivered as that milestone's evidence, by the contractor's agent (`milestone_evidence`), so the client releases the milestone payment on a measurement. A failed run delivers nothing.
recipes.needs: A contract (contracts v2) whose provider is the proxy's agent; the SFTP account's key and the server's host key (`known_hosts`). Install the `proxy-sftp` extra. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run --once     # what it would send, sending nothing
recipes.try_it: `python fake/fake_logger.py /exports --contract <id> --milestone 0 --strength 41.5` writes a passed run (35 MPa is the limit; `--strength 30` writes a failed one). Then:
recipes.check: The contract shows the milestone delivered, its deliverable carrying the run; a failed run delivers nothing; each file read is moved into `done/` on the server. The source polls every `poll_seconds` (60): for a one-off run (`--once`) set `poll_seconds: 0`, or `--once` never ends; the server account needs write access to the export folder for the move (without it the file stays, is named in the log, and is not read twice).
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# KEYSTONE (the construction blueprint): the site's sensor logger exports each test run as a CSV to an SFTP server; the
# run's acceptance row (the measured result against its limit, for one contract milestone) is delivered as that
# milestone's evidence on TheProtocol, by the contractor's agent, so the client releases the milestone payment on a
# measurement rather than an e-mail. The measurement rows of the run stay in the export; only the acceptance row is
# evidence, and only a passed run has one (a failed run's last row is a rejection).
#
# The logger side: runs-<run>.csv in /exports on the SFTP server, each with a .done marker once complete
# (fake/fake_logger.py writes such runs). The contract and its milestone are named in the export's acceptance row.
version: 1
name: keystone-sensors
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/keystone-state.db
sources:
  logger:
    type: sftp
    config:
      host: sftp.site.local
      port: 22
      username: tp-proxy
      private_key: file:/run/secrets/sftp_key
      known_hosts: /run/secrets/sftp_known_hosts
      path: /exports
      suffix: .csv
      require_marker: .done          # a run is read only once the logger has written its .done marker
      id_field: row_id
actions:
  deliver:
    type: milestone_evidence
    config: {}                       # the contract and the milestone come from the acceptance row
    limits: {per_minute: 30}
sinks: {}
mappings:
  - name: acceptance
    version: 1
    from: logger
    to: deliver
    when: {path: $.payload.data.kind, equals: acceptance}
    fields:
      contract_id: $.payload.data.contract_id
      seq: $.payload.data.milestone
      test: $.payload.data.test
      result: $.payload.data.result
      measured: $.payload.data.value
      limit: $.payload.data.limit
      unit: $.payload.data.unit
      run: $.payload.data.run_id
      at: $.payload.data.at
retry: {first_s: 5, max_s: 600, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

recipes.name: LYCEUM
recipes.summary: awarded credentials from the student-record export
recipes.legacy: The student-record system exports the credentials it has awarded as a CSV (`award_id`, a pseudonymous `holder_pseudonym`, `credential`, `eqf_level`, `ects`, `awarded_on`, `status`) into `/data/sis-out`.
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each AWARDED row becomes a `lyceum.credential_awarded` attestation a verifier can check without asking the school. A REVOKED row is left out: revocation is a deliberate act in the console.
recipes.needs: An agent with the `attestor` role. The export names no student by name or birth date. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: the folder is watched, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/fake_sis.py ./sis-out --count 5` writes one export (its last row REVOKED). Then:
recipes.check: The attestations are on the agent's record, one per awarded row. A file is read once it has not changed for `settle_seconds` (2): a `--once` run started while the export is still being written passes over it, and the next run reads it. The export folder is listed again every 30 seconds (`poll_seconds: 30`), so a file dropped while the proxy runs is read too; without it the source lists the folder once and finishes, which is what a `--once` run is. For a `--once` try, set `poll_seconds: 0` in the spec for that run.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# LYCEUM (the education blueprint): the student-record system exports the credentials it has awarded as a CSV; each
# awarded credential becomes a signed attestation on TheProtocol that a verifier can check later without asking the
# school. A withdrawn award in the same export (status REVOKED) is left out: revocation is a deliberate act in the
# console, never a side effect of an export.
#
# The student-record side: credentials-<date>.csv with the header line the fake writes (fake/fake_sis.py) into
# /data/sis-out. The holder is named by a pseudonymous id, never by name or birth date.
version: 1
name: lyceum-credentials
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/lyceum-state.db
sources:
  sis:
    type: filedrop
    config: {path: /data/sis-out, suffix: .csv, id_field: award_id, settle_seconds: 2, poll_seconds: 30}
actions:
  issue:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: lyceum.credential_awarded}
    limits: {per_minute: 120}
sinks: {}
mappings:
  - name: credential
    version: 1
    from: sis
    to: issue
    when: {path: $.payload.data.status, equals: AWARDED}
    fields:
      award: $.payload.data.award_id
      holder: $.payload.data.holder_pseudonym
      credential: $.payload.data.credential
      level: $.payload.data.eqf_level
      ects: $.payload.data.ects
      awarded_on: $.payload.data.awarded_on
      institution: LYCEUM-DEMO
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

recipes.name: MERIDIAN
recipes.summary: order intents in, signed evidence to the ERP folder
recipes.legacy: The order-management system exports its order intents as JSON arrays into a folder (`/data/oms-out`).
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each RELEASED intent becomes a `meridian.order_intent` attestation; the ERP's import folder (`/data/erp-in`) receives the hash-chained evidence of every intent, its manifest signed by the proxy's key.
recipes.needs: An agent holding the `attestor` role (the attestation's `reputation.signal`), and an evidence signing key (`tp-proxy keygen /run/secrets/evidence.pem`). Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: the folder is watched, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/fake_oms.py ./oms-out --batch 1 --count 5` writes one export (one HELD intent among them, not attested). Then:
recipes.check: `tp-proxy verify /data/erp-in --key <public key>` checks the ERP's copy offline (`tp-proxy keygen` printed the public key); a changed line or another signer fails it with exit code 1 and names the line. A file is read once it has not changed for `settle_seconds` (2): a `--once` run started while the export is still being written passes over it, and the next run reads it. The export folder is listed again every 30 seconds (`poll_seconds: 30`), so a file dropped while the proxy runs is read too; without it the source lists the folder once and finishes, which is what a `--once` run is. For a `--once` try, set `poll_seconds: 0` in the spec for that run.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# MERIDIAN (the industrial-procurement blueprint): the order-management system drops its order intents as JSON files;
# each intent becomes a signed attestation on TheProtocol, and the ERP's import folder receives the hash-chained,
# signed evidence of every intent the proxy carried (checked offline with tp-proxy verify).
#
# The OMS side: an export job writes intents-<batch>.json (a JSON array) into /data/oms-out; the fake in fake/ does
# the same. The ERP side reads /data/erp-in. Credentials come from the agent's starter files, never this file.
version: 1
name: meridian-oms
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/meridian-state.db
sources:
  oms:
    type: filedrop
    # settle_seconds: an export is read only once the file has stopped growing
    config: {path: /data/oms-out, format: json, suffix: .json, id_field: intent_id, settle_seconds: 2, poll_seconds: 30}
actions:
  attest:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: meridian.order_intent}
    limits: {per_minute: 120}
sinks:
  erp:
    type: evidence
    config: {dir: /data/erp-in, signing_key: file:/run/secrets/evidence.pem}
mappings:
  - name: intent
    version: 1
    from: oms
    to: attest
    when: {path: $.payload.data.status, equals: RELEASED}
    fields:
      intent: $.payload.data.intent_id
      order: $.payload.data.order_no
      buyer: $.payload.data.buyer
      sku: $.payload.data.sku
      quantity: $.payload.data.qty
      released_at: $.payload.data.released_at
  - name: intent-evidence
    version: 1
    from: oms
    to: erp
    when: {path: $.payload.data.status, equals: RELEASED}
    fields:
      intent: $.payload.data.intent_id
      order: $.payload.data.order_no
      sku: $.payload.data.sku
      quantity: $.payload.data.qty
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

table.out: signed evidence to the ERP folder

recipes.name: SCRIVENER
recipes.summary: matter events in, the DMS's evidence out
recipes.legacy: The practice-management system posts each matter event (opened, a filing with the filed document's SHA-256, a deadline met, closed), HMAC-signed with `PMS_HMAC`, to `/in/matters`.
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each event becomes a `scrivener.matter_event` attestation, and the document-management system's import folder receives the signed, hash-chained history of the matter: a court or an auditor checks it offline.
recipes.needs: An agent with the `attestor` role; an evidence signing key; `PMS_HMAC`. To mirror the evidence to an SFTP server, set the evidence sink's `mirror` (the `proxy-sftp` extra). Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: a receiver never finishes, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/fake_pms.py http://127.0.0.1:8711/in/matters --matter M-2026-0042` posts one matter's four events. Then:
recipes.check: `tp-proxy verify /data/dms-import --key <public key>` names any changed, removed or moved line.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# SCRIVENER (the legal-services blueprint): the practice-management system posts each matter event (opened, a filing
# made, a deadline met, closed) to the proxy; every event becomes a signed attestation on TheProtocol, and the document
# management system's import folder receives the hash-chained, signed evidence of the matter's history, checked offline
# with tp-proxy verify (a court or an auditor needs no network and no trust in the firm's own systems).
#
# The practice-management side: POST /in/matters, HMAC-signed with PMS_HMAC (fake/fake_pms.py). The DMS side reads
# /data/dms-import; mirror it to an SFTP server with the evidence sink's mirror setting (the proxy-sftp extra).
version: 1
name: scrivener-matters
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/scrivener-state.db
sources:
  pms:
    type: webhook
    config: {listen: "0.0.0.0:8711", path: /in/matters, id_field: event_id, secret: env:PMS_HMAC}
actions:
  attest:
    type: attestation
    config: {attestation_type: scrivener.matter_event}
    limits: {per_minute: 120}
sinks:
  dms:
    type: evidence
    config: {dir: /data/dms-import, signing_key: file:/run/secrets/evidence.pem}
mappings:
  - name: matter-event
    version: 1
    from: pms
    to: attest
    fields:
      matter: $.payload.matter_id
      event: $.payload.type
      document: {path: $.payload.document_sha256, default: null}
      by: $.payload.fee_earner
      at: $.payload.at
  - name: matter-evidence
    version: 1
    from: pms
    to: dms
    fields:
      matter: $.payload.matter_id
      event: $.payload.type
      document: {path: $.payload.document_sha256, default: null}
      at: $.payload.at
retry: {first_s: 2, max_s: 300, attempts: 8}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}

recipes.name: TRUNK
recipes.legacy: The mediation system rates each interconnect event into its settlement table (`settlement_events`, cursor `event_seq`): the partner carrier's agent, the minutes and the charge.
recipes.on_theprotocol: Each RATED event is settled as it happens, a payment to the partner's agent under the operator's Cockpit mandate, never above the action's `max_amount` or `per_day`, nor the mandate's limits; finance gets a CSV journal (or ISO 20022 camt.053) of what settled, booked from the registry's own `payment.settled` notice (each line names its settlement), so a payment the proxy refused or the registry held back has no line. A DISPUTED event is neither paid nor booked.
recipes.needs: A Cockpit mandate (`a2a.pay`) issued by the operator's owner, named in `mandate:`; a webhook in the console (Developer, Webhooks) for `payment.settled` to this proxy's receiver (`/in/theprotocol`, its secret as `TP_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), and the proxy agent's DID in the `book-settled` mapping's `when` (the owner's webhook carries every payment of the owner's agents); the agent's IRONKEY spend cap at or under it; the payee agents bonded where the registry enforces the bond. SQLite needs no extra; PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server take the `proxy-sql` extras. Credentials come from the agent's starter files (`.env`, `.env.secret`) by reference; none is written in the spec.
commands: tp-proxy run proxy.yaml --dry-run            # what it would send, sending nothing (Ctrl-C to stop: a receiver never finishes, so --once does not end here)
recipes.try_it: `python fake/fake_mediation.py ./mediation.db --partner-did <the partner's agent> --count 5` rates five events (one DISPUTED). Then:
recipes.check: Each payment's settlement is on both agents' records; the journal holds one debit per settled payment, its text the settlement's transaction id; a refused one is in `tp-proxy dead` and not in the journal; the ledgers' supply delta stays 0.
recipes.proxy_yaml:
# TRUNK (the telecom blueprint): the mediation system rates each interconnect event and writes it to its settlement
# table; every rated event is settled on TheProtocol as it happens, a payment to the partner carrier's agent under the
# operator's Cockpit mandate (nothing is paid without one, and never above the action's max_amount or the mandate's
# limits), and finance gets a CSV journal (or camt.053, for systems that read account statements) of what SETTLED: each
# line comes from TheProtocol's own payment.settled notice (the registry's webhook) and names its settlement, so a
# payment refused or held back (over max_amount, outside the mandate) has no line. An event the mediation system
# disputes (status DISPUTED) is neither paid nor booked.
#
# The mediation side: the table settlement_events, its cursor column event_seq (fake/fake_mediation.py writes such
# rows into an SQLite file; PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server work the same with the proxy-sql extras). The mandate: the
# operator's owner issues it in the console (Cockpit, a2a.pay) and names it here; the agent's IRONKEY spend cap must
# sit at or under it, or the payment action does not start.
version: 1
name: trunk-settlement
registry: https://api.theprotocol.cloud
identity:
  agent_did: env:AGENT_DID
  client_id: env:CLIENT_ID
  client_secret: env:CLIENT_SECRET
state: /data/trunk-state.db
sources:
  mediation:
    type: sqlpoll
    config: {engine: sqlite, path: /data/mediation.db, table: settlement_events, cursor: event_seq, poll_seconds: 5}
  theprotocol:
    # the registry's webhook (console: Developer, Webhooks; event payment.settled) for the journal: it books what
    # settled, never what was only rated (a payment refused or held back has no line)
    type: theprotocol_events
    config: {listen: "0.0.0.0:8712", path: /in/theprotocol, secret: env:TP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, events: [payment.settled]}
actions:
  settle:
    type: payment
    # your mandate's id (lm_...), from the console; max_amount: the most one event may settle
    config: {mandate: lm_yourmandate, max_amount: 25, per_day: 2000}
    limits: {per_minute: 120}
sinks:
  finance:
    type: journal
    config: {dir: /data/finance-journal, format: csv, account: {id: TRUNK-INTERCONNECT, currency: ECU}}
mappings:
  - name: settle-event
    version: 1
    from: mediation
    to: settle
    when: {path: $.payload.status, equals: RATED}
    fields:
      payee: $.payload.partner_agent_did
      amount: $.payload.charge
      event: $.payload.event_id
      partner: $.payload.partner_code
      minutes: $.payload.minutes
  - name: book-settled
    version: 1
    from: theprotocol
    to: finance
    # the owner's webhook carries every payment of the owner's agents: book this proxy's agent's own (its DID here)
    when: {path: $.payload.caller_did, equals: "did:theprotocol:your-proxy-agent"}
    fields:
      amount: $.payload.amount
      direction: debit
      currency: $.payload.currency
      counterparty: $.payload.target_agent_did
      text: $.payload.settlement_tx_id
retry: {first_s: 5, max_s: 600, attempts: 8}
breaker: {refusals: 3, failures: 10, cooldown_s: 60}
service: {listen: "127.0.0.1:9108"}
